title: Turkey ham, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey ham is cooked turkey meat, usually skinless, sliced thinly and packaged in vacuum‑sealed bags or sold as deli‑style slices. It is commonly used in sandwiches, salads and quick snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey ham contains less fat than traditional pork ham.
Turkey is one of the most popular poultry meats in the United States, where its meat is often processed into ham.
Vacuum packaging extends shelf life to several weeks without added preservatives.
Low‑sodium versions are available for those watching salt intake.
Thin slices are convenient for fast‑assembly sandwiches and wraps.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Turkey ham provides less saturated fat than pork ham, making it a better choice for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving delivers about 20 g of high‑quality protein essential for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Reduced sodium in diet versions
items.content: Some products are formulated with less salt, which can help manage blood pressure.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey ham supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and folate, supporting metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Selenium and zinc
items.content: These minerals contribute to antioxidant protection and immune function.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey meat.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Regular turkey ham can be high in salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain packages contain nitrites or other preservatives; those sensitive should avoid them.

items.title: Bacterial growth if mishandled
items.content: Improper refrigeration can allow salmonella or listeria to develop.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turkey ham can be eaten cold in sandwiches, salads, wraps, or added to hot dishes such as pasta, omelets, and stir‑fries. The thin slices make it a quick, ready‑to‑eat snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepackaged turkey ham refrigerated at 0‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Frozen product can be stored up to 2 months; thaw in the refrigerator before use.
